subtitle: "Forecasting for Time Series (PPLEDBA)"
author: "Prof. Dae-Jin Lee (daelee@faculty.ie.edu)"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab13", title = "Prophet vs ARIMA")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "Choose between Prophet, ETS, and ARIMA using:",
  q2 = "If a flexible model cannot beat SNAIVE on the hold-out, you should:",
  q3 = "Prophet is best thought of as:",
  q4 = "Which Beer model would you recommend to a non-technical manager, and why?"
)
```

## What you will do

Bake-off rules. Prophet is optional and is not required to finish the questions.

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `fpp3`, `learnr`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("Hold-out accuracy on the original scale, plus residual checks", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Training AICc across all families"),
  answer("Whichever model has more parameters"),
  answer("The last model you fit"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("Ship the simpler SNAIVE forecast", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Add more harmonics until AICc falls"),
  answer("Ignore the hold-out"),
  answer("Difference twice"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("A curve (trend + season + holidays) with its own fitting stack", correct = TRUE),
  answer("A special case of ARIMA(0,1,1)"),
  answer("A replacement for every ETS model"),
  answer("A test for stationarity"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Name one model and one hold-out or residual reason.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Answer the questions above first, type your name, download the `.txt`, and upload it.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
